    New Zealand–India trade is moving at pace. Two-way trade has nearly doubled since 2022 – from $2.0 billion to $3.9 billion. India is now New Zealand’s 11th largest bilateral trading partner. The historic visit of Indian Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to New Zealand this weekend – the first by an Indian PM in 40 years – and the announcement of a new Strategic Partnership and ambition to double trade by 2030, build on that momentum. Read more here:https://lnkd.in/d85dMw5J NZTE was proud to support the visit, helping to bring together over 50 New Zealand and Indian business leaders to explore opportunities for partnership, investment and commercial growth. Once in force, the New Zealand–India Free Trade Agreement will open even more doors across a range of sectors where New Zealand businesses bring world-class capability. NZTE is helping more exporters prepare, connect and grow in India than ever before.     Great to see New Zealand agritech getting coverage for its growing momentum in Latin America following Field Days Latin America which New Zealand Trade and Enterprise held in the Los Lagos region in Chile in April. From what we’re seeing on the ground, the demand from dairy producers in Latin America is very real, particularly for solutions that deliver practical gains in productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Chile continues to play a key role here, acting as a gateway market for the region, where New Zealand technologies can demonstrate value and build a platform for broader LATAM expansion. Following Field Days Latin America, Gonzalo Riquelme supported a delegation from South America to Fieldays®NZ which demonstrated the value of connecting producers directly with New Zealand’s agritech ecosystem. At the same time, one message continues to come through clearly - success in LATAM is not just about great technology, it’s about understanding local context and building trusted, long-term partnerships. For NZ agritech companies, this is where the opportunity really lies. With the right approach, LATAM is not just a growth market, it’s a region where solutions can scale and deliver real impact. Exciting to see this momentum continue. https://lnkd.in/dwkaWzjH #AgriTech #NZTE #LATAM Stephen Blair Gonzalo Riquelme Steve Chappell Rebecca Foy

    New Zealand exports to India topped NZ$2 billion in the year ended December 2025. As the recently signed New Zealand–India Free Trade Agreement moves through the parliamentary process, now is the time to look more closely at the export opportunities ahead. India offers real scale, with regional differences in culture, regulation and customer behaviour. Getting clear on your target segment, route to market and business model can make all the difference. If you are exploring India or already on the ground, NZTE’s India Market Guide brings together practical guidance to support your next step. It covers market entry strategy, common exporter challenges and how to build the right partnerships. Start here: https://lnkd.in/dCdvJX4z #India #MarketEntry #RouteToMarket #ExportInsights #myNZTE

    🧬 New Zealand biotech is back on the global stage—and making a strong impression. 🌎✨ At BIO International Convention 2026 this week, New Zealand Trade and Enterprise showcased nine leading Kiwi organizations at the New Zealand Pavilion, including BioOra, Optimal Clinical Trials + New Zealand Clinical Research, HiRO - Harvest Integrated Research Organization, Hugh Green Technology Centre at the Malaghan Institute, Izon Science, Momentum Clinical Research, New Zealand Pharmaceuticals Limited, Novotech, and UniServices. Across four days of meetings, panels, and networking with over 20,000 global biotech leaders, discussions centered on the themes driving the sector forward: partnerships, clinical research, investment, advanced manufacturing, and pathways to commercialization. Beyond the show activity, NZTE hosted a networking happy hour at the pavilion and co-hosted a reception with partners including Bridgewest Group, BioTech New Zealand, and Australian state and federal organizations, creating valuable opportunities to strengthen relationships and spark new collaborations. 🤝🔬 One of the strongest signals from the week was the value of showing up collectively. When companies, research organizations, and industry partners tell a broader New Zealand story together, it helps amplify the scale, capability, and credibility of the entire ecosystem. As global demand grows for breakthrough therapies, clinical research expertise, and advanced biotech capabilities, New Zealand continues to demonstrate that world-class innovation can come from anywhere. “10 Kiwi CROs. One big biotech story at BIO San Diego” - Charles Haddrell
